walkthrough:
**Identify the functional groups in X**

X has three functional groups to track. There is an aldehyde $\text{CHO}$, a ketone $\text{COCH}_3$, and an alkene C=C in the ring.

Keep them separate in your mind: $$\text{X = aldehyde + ketone + alkene}$$

**Apply the mild oxidising agent to get Y**

A mild oxidising agent is selective. It oxidises an aldehyde to a carboxylic acid, but it is not strong enough to oxidise a ketone.

Reaction: $$\text{R-CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{mild [O]}} \text{R-CO}_2\text{H}$$
So Y contains $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ and unchanged $\text{COCH}_3$, with the C=C still present.

**Apply NaBH4 to get Z**

$\text{NaBH}_4$ is a selective reducing agent. It reduces ketones to secondary alcohols, but it does not reduce carboxylic acids and does not reduce C=C double bonds.

Reaction: $$\text{R-COCH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{NaBH}_4} \text{R-CH(OH)CH}_3$$
So the $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ stays as $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, the ketone becomes $\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, and the ring alkene remains. That matches the structure with $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, $\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ and a double bond.

options.A: Correct. The aldehyde was oxidised to $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, the ketone was then reduced to $\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, and the C=C double bond is correctly retained because neither reagent attacks alkenes.
options.B: Incorrect. This shows $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ from reduction of the aldehyde. A mild oxidising agent oxidises $\text{CHO}$ to $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, it does not leave it to be reduced to a primary alcohol.
options.C: Incorrect. This has two errors. It shows $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ instead of $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, and it shows a saturated ring. $\text{NaBH}_4$ does not reduce C=C bonds, so the alkene should still be there.
options.D: Incorrect. The functional groups $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ and $\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ are right, but the ring is shown saturated. Neither a mild oxidising agent nor $\text{NaBH}_4$ reduces an alkene, so the double bond must remain.
